catalog_quote: [p. 812] Ударение силовое, падает на последний слог слова: manús ‛человекʼ, ‛муж-чинаʼ, ‛мужʼ, mančʰáv ‛рыбаʼ, čahrí ‛ситоʼ, čʰətár ‛четыреʼ, buhú ‛многоʼ. 5.1.1. Структура слога не изучена. 5.1.2. Типы чередований не изучены. [p. 816] О т р и ц а н и е во всех видо-временних формах, кроме императива, осуществляется с помощью частицы na ‛неʼ: ná ku lekʰem ‛не вижуʼ, na lekʰecʰir ‛ты не увиделʼ, na eir lekʰer ‛ты не виделʼ, na lekʰes piti ‛ты не увидишьʼ. В императиве используется запретительная частица má ‛неʼ: ma lekʰe ‛не смотриʼ, ma lekʰekʰ ‛не смотритеʼ. Обе частицы являются «исконными» грамматическими элементами. [translation] Stress is dynamic (force stress) and falls on the last syllable of the word: manús 'person, man, husband', mančʰáv 'fish', čahrí 'sieve', čʰətár 'four', buhú 'much'. 5.1.1. Syllable structure has not been studied. 5.1.2. Types of alternation have not been studied. [p. 816] Negation in all aspect-tense forms except the imperative is by the particle na 'not': ná ku lekʰem 'I do not see', ...; in the imperative the prohibitive particle má 'not' is used: ma lekʰe 'do not look', ma lekʰekʰ 'do not look (pl.)'. Both particles are 'native' grammatical elements.
world_status: statement found in an open source

new_statements.translation: Stress is dynamic (expiratory) and falls on the last syllable of the word: manús 'person, man, husband', mančʰáv 'fish', čahrí 'sieve', čʰətár 'four', buhú 'much, many'.

new_statements.second_reader_evidence: Opened (890 pp., text layer present; iling-ran.ru whole-volume PDF of Jazyki mira: Novye indoarijskie jazyki, 2011). extracted text of PDF pp. 811-813 shows V.S. Voskanian, 'Lomavren jazyk' beginning on printed p. 811; on p. 812, directly under the consonant table in sec. 5.1.0 'Fonologicheskie svedenija', the sentence reads exactly: 'Ударение силовое, падает на последний слог слова: manús ‛человекʼ, ‛мужчинаʼ, ‛мужʼ, mančʰáv ‛рыбаʼ, čahrí ‛ситоʼ, čʰətár ‛четыреʼ, buhú ‛многоʼ.' (only difference from the report is the line-break hyphen in муж-чина). This is followed by 5.1.1 'Структура слога не изучена' and 5.1.2 'Типы чередований не изучены', as the reader said. Reading fixed: final syllab…
new_statements.rule_in_words: Word stress is fixed on the final syllable of the word (as in the Western Armenian grammatical matrix of the language); examples are bare citation forms.
new_statements.exceptions: None stated explicitly. The sketch adds that syllable structure and alternations are 'not studied' (5.1.1-5.1.2). On p. 816 the negative particle na and prohibitive ma are printed with an acute in examples (ná ku lekʰem 'I do not see', má), suggesting these proclitic particles attract stress as in Armenian, but no rule is formulated; behaviour of the enclitic definite article -ə/-n is not discussed.
new_statements.domain_note: Word-level statement ('последний слог слова'), illustrated with isolated citation forms; the sketch describes the Armenia/Georgia dialect of Lomavren (sec. 2.0), whose speakers are L1 Armenian and use Lomavren as a secret register.
new_statements.identity_note: Voskanian 2011 explicitly describes the Lomavren variety of Armenia and southern Georgia (Yerevan, Gyumri, Akhalkalaki, Akhaltsikhe), not the Turkish (Kars/Artvin) variety; this is the variety Glottolog files under loma1235 (ISO rmi). Lomavren is an Armenian-grammar mixed language/secret register whose speakers are L1 (Western-type) Armenian speakers; the final-stress rule matches the Armenian matrix.

new_statements.quote: 64. Der hauptnachdruck trifft, wie die ausdrücklichen angaben in XV zeigen, die letzte silbe des wortes, sofern diese nicht den reduzierten vokal ə enthält und ein anderer volltönender im worte vorkommt. Einer jedesmaligen angabe des accents bedarf es demnach nicht. [p. 83, § 64; verified against the page image. Also p. 84, § 69:] Der vokal ə liegt nur in einem einzigen beleg als vollbetonter vokal vor, und zwar in kʻəl 'fett, schmalz, butter' (§ 58) = prkr. ... Ausserdem erscheint er dreimal für unbetontes ...
new_statements.translation: 64. The main stress falls, as the explicit indications in [source] XV show, on the last syllable of the word, provided that this syllable does not contain the reduced vowel ə while another full vowel occurs in the word. A case-by-case marking of the accent is therefore unnecessary. [§ 69:] The vowel ə occurs as a fully stressed vowel in only a single attestation, namely in kʻəl 'fat, lard, butter'; otherwise it appears three times for unstressed [Prakrit vowels] ...

new_statements.second_reader_evidence: Opened (1186 pp; the PDF's metadata gives the title = Zapiski Imp. Akad. nauk po Ist.-fil. otd. / Memoires de l'Acad. imp. des sciences, Classe hist.-phil.). Volume TOC (the scanned text) lists 'No 5. Franz Nikolaus Finck. Die Sprache der armenischen Zigeuner'; the monograph title page (scanned lines ~13700-13730) reads 'Tome VIII no 5.. DIE SPRACHE DER ARMENISCHEN ZIGEUNER von Franz Nikolaus Finck.. St.-Petersbourg 1907'. PDF page 321 = printed p. 83 (running head 'DIE SPRACHE DER ARMENISCHEN ZIGEUNER. 83'); I viewed the saved page image and read § 64 verbatim: 'Der hauptnachdruck trifft, wie die ausdrücklichen angaben in XV zeigen, die letzte silbe des wortes, sofern diese nicht den reduz…
new_statements.relation_note: Same placement as the catalog record (final stress = final stress) and as Voskanian 2011 (Ударение.. падает на последний слог). Finck adds a vowel-quality condition absent from both: a final syllable containing reduced ə is unstressed if the word has a full vowel, and stress marking is redundant because placement is predictable. He is also explicit that the placement is documented only in source XV (Erzurum speakers, Lehmann's list), the other sources not marking accent at all.
new_statements.rule_in_words: Primary stress falls on the final syllable of the word; the only stated exception is that a final syllable whose vowel is the reduced ə does not take the stress when the word contains another full vowel (stress then retracts to that full vowel). Because the rule is predictable, Finck does not mark accent in his normalized transcription. The rule rests on the explicit accent marks in source XV (C. F. Lehmann's list of 83 items from four Gypsies in and near Erzurum).
new_statements.secondary_stress: Not mentioned; only the 'hauptnachdruck' (main stress) is discussed.
new_statements.exceptions: Final syllables with reduced ə are skipped in favour of a full vowel elsewhere in the word (§ 64); ə carries full stress in only one attested word, kʻəl 'fat, lard, butter' (§ 69, p. 84), where no full vowel is available.
new_statements.identity_note: Finck's monograph compiles all records then available of the Armenian Gypsies (Bosha/Lom) of Erzurum, Zalka (emigrants from Erzurum, 1828), Tokat, Alexandropol (Gyumri) and Armenian-script sources (Vanthsean, Phaphazean, Lalajean, Dschanikean). The stress rule itself is stated on the basis of the explicit accent marks in source XV only: C. F. Lehmann's list of 83 words, phrases and sentences from four Gypsies in and near Erzurum (Erserum), i.e. the Erzurum variety around 1900. Voskanian 2011 describes the Lomavren of Armenia; both agree on final stress.

As a substitute I spot-checked the two earlier-saved works logged as silent in : (1) Finck 1907 JGLS article 'Die Grundzüge des armenisch-zigeunerischen Sprachbaus' (printed p. 48, the scanned text): the only stress remark is that possible differences of Betonung in compounds 'are not evident from the records' and cannot be decided; no placement rule - correctly logged as silent on placement.
